q.q: The reason why (A) / he failed the exam (B) / is because (C) / he did not study hard. (D)
q.x: The phrases 'the reason' and 'because' are redundant when used together. Use 'that' instead of 'because' after 'is'.

q.q: Had the server configuration been optimized earlier, (A) / the latency issues that plagued the database (B) / would not have persisted for so long (C) / than it actually did (D).
o: Had the server configuration been optimized earlier,
the latency issues that plagued the database
would not have persisted for so long
q.x: The phrase 'so long' should be followed by 'as it did' in this comparative context, or simply 'as they did' to match the plural 'issues'. The use of 'than' is grammatically incorrect here.

q.q: Being a rainy day, (A) / I could not go to the office (B) / and decided to work (C) / from the comfort of my home. (D)
q.x: The error is in part A. This is a dangling participle error. The subject 'I' cannot 'be a rainy day'. The correct structure should be 'It being a rainy day, I could not go...'.

q.q: She is (A) / more taller than (B) / any other student (C) / in the class. (D)
q.x: Double comparatives are grammatically incorrect. Use 'taller than' instead of 'more taller than'.

q.q: The committee is divided (A) / in their opinion (B) / regarding the new policy (C) / implemented last month. (D)
q.x: When a collective noun is divided in opinion, the verb and pronoun should be plural. It should be 'The committee are divided in their opinion'.

q.q: Not only the principal (A) / but also the teachers (B) / was present in the (C) / emergency meeting held yesterday. (D)
q.x: When using 'not only... but also', the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. Since 'teachers' is plural, 'was' should be 'were'.

q.q: Each of the students (A) / who have registered for the seminar (B) / are required to submit (C) / their assignments by Friday. (D)
q.x: The subject of the sentence is 'Each', which is singular. Therefore, the verb must be 'is required' instead of 'are required'.

q.q: Unless you do not submit the code repository access, (A) / the audit team will not be able to (B) / verify the compliance of the software (C) / with international security standards (D).
o: Unless you do not submit the code repository access,
the audit team will not be able to
verify the compliance of the software
q.x: The word 'unless' is already negative. Adding 'do not' creates a double negative. It should read 'Unless you submit the code repository access'.

q.q: One of the most significant challenges that (A) / our engineering team faces today (B) / involve scaling the infrastructure (C) / to support concurrent user sessions (D).
o: One of the most significant challenges that
q.x: The subject of the sentence is 'One' (of the challenges), which is singular. The verb 'involve' must be singular as 'involves'.

q.q: Each of the students who participated in the debate (A) / have been awarded a certificate (B) / for their exceptional performance (C) / during the final round. (D)
q.x: The error is in part B. When 'each' is the subject of the sentence, the verb must be singular. Therefore, 'has' should replace 'have', despite the plural 'students' appearing in the preceding clause.

q.q: I would have visited you (A) / if I knew (B) / that you were (C) / hospitalized for a week. (D)
q.x: This is a third conditional sentence structure. 'If I had known' is the correct past perfect form to match 'would have visited'.

q.q: He is more smarter (A) / than his brother (B) / when it comes to (C) / solving complex puzzles (D).
q.x: Double comparatives are incorrect in English. It should be 'smarter' instead of 'more smarter'.

q.q: The news (A) / of his demise (B) / were communicated (C) / to the family immediately. (D)
q.x: 'News' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb. It should be 'was communicated' instead of 'were communicated'.

q.q: It is I who is responsible (A) / for the mess created in the laboratory (B) / and I am prepared to face the consequences (C) / of my actions. (D)
q.x: The error is in part A. When a relative pronoun (who) follows a personal pronoun (I), the verb must agree with the antecedent. Since the antecedent is 'I', the verb should be 'am' instead of 'is'.

q.q: Every boy and (A) / every girl have (B) / received the invitation (C) / for the event (D).
q.x: When two singular subjects are preceded by 'every', the verb must be singular. Therefore, 'have' should be 'has'.

q.q: The information provided by the witnesses (A) / were not sufficient enough (B) / to convict the accused (C) / in the court of law. (D)
q.x: The error is in part B. 'Information' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb, so 'was' should be used instead of 'were'. Additionally, 'sufficient enough' is redundant.

q.q: It is high time the administration took strict measures (A) / against those who habitually bypass security protocols (B) / and undermines the integrity of the (C) / company's private cloud infrastructure (D).
o: It is high time the administration took strict measures
against those who habitually bypass security protocols
and undermines the integrity of the
q.x: The verb 'undermines' must be parallel to the verb 'bypass'. Since 'bypass' refers to the antecedent 'those' (plural), 'undermines' should be 'undermine'.

q.q: The information provided (A) / by the clerk (B) / were not accurate (C) / for our records (D).
q.x: 'Information' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb. 'Were' should be 'was'.

q.q: Hardly had I stepped out (A) / of the office (B) / than it started (C) / raining heavily. (D)
q.x: The correlative conjunction for 'Hardly' is 'when', not 'than'. 'Than' is used with 'no sooner'.

q.q: One of the most (A) / talented students (B) / who has ever attended (C) / this university are graduating today. (D)
q.x: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the antecedent 'students', which is plural. Therefore, 'has' should be 'have'.

q.q: It is I (A) / who is responsible (B) / for the mess created (C) / during the event. (D)
q.x: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the antecedent 'I'. Therefore, the verb must be 'am' instead of 'is'.

q.q: Hardly had I stepped out of the office (A) / than it started raining heavily (B) / leaving me in a state of complete helplessness (C) / as I had forgotten my umbrella. (D)
q.x: The error is in part B. The correlative conjunction 'Hardly' must be followed by 'when', not 'than'. 'Than' is used with 'no sooner'.

q.q: Scarcely had he stepped (A) / out of the office (B) / when it began to rain (C) / heavily and unexpectedly. (D)
q.x: There is no error in this sentence. 'Scarcely' is correctly followed by 'had he' and the correlative conjunction 'when'.

q.q: Neither the head of the department nor the senior professors (A) / are willing to accept the proposal (B) / because it lacks the necessary empirical evidence (C) / required for the project approval. (D)
q.x: The error lies in part A. According to the rule of proximity, when subjects are joined by 'neither/nor', the verb must agree with the closer subject. Since 'senior professors' is plural, the verb 'are' in part B is correct; however, if the subject order were reversed, the verb would change. Actually, in this sentence, the structure is correct, but 'head' is singular and 'professors' is plural, so 'neither the head... nor the senior professors are' is grammatically sound. Wait, the error is actually in the choice of 'are'; the proximity rule confirms 'are' is correct. Let's re-evaluate: Actually, there is no error in this sentence.

q.q: Little he knew that the patch released yesterday (A) / would inadvertently introduce a vulnerability (B) / that could expose sensitive user credentials (C) / to unauthorized external entities (D).
o: Little he knew that the patch released yesterday
that could expose sensitive user credentials
q.x: When a sentence begins with a negative adverbial like 'Little', inversion is required. It should be 'Little did he know', not 'Little he knew'.

q.q: She is one of those people (A) / who likes to (B) / gossip about others (C) / behind their backs. (D)
o: She is one of those people
q.x: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'people', which is plural. Therefore, 'likes' should be 'like'.

q.q: If I was you, (A) / I would have accepted the offer (B) / without any hesitation (C) / regarding the salary package. (D)
q.x: The error is in part A. This is a hypothetical condition (subjunctive mood), which requires the use of 'were' instead of 'was' regardless of the subject. The correct phrase is 'If I were you'.

q.q: The committee is divided (A) / in their opinion (B) / regarding the new policy (C) / proposed by the chairman. (D)
q.x: When a collective noun like 'committee' is divided in opinion, it is treated as plural. The verb should be 'are divided' instead of 'is divided'.

q.q: The documentation provided by the vendor (A) / is so poorly written that neither the user (B) / nor the developer are able to understand (C) / the API integration requirements (D).
o: The documentation provided by the vendor
is so poorly written that neither the user
nor the developer are able to understand
q.x: In 'neither/nor' constructions, the verb must agree with the closer subject. Since 'developer' is singular, the verb must be 'is', not 'are'.

q.q: If I was you (A) / I would not (B) / accept that offer (C) / from the company (D).
q.x: In conditional sentences expressing a hypothetical situation, 'were' is used instead of 'was'. This is the subjunctive mood.

q.q: One of the most (A) / intelligent student (B) / in the class (C) / has cleared the exam (D).
q.x: The phrase 'one of the' is always followed by a plural noun. Therefore, 'student' should be 'students'.

q.q: The furniture (A) / in this apartment (B) / are quite old (C) / and need urgent repair. (D)
q.x: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb. 'Are' should be 'is' and 'need' should be 'needs'.

q.q: I have finished (A) / my lunch an (B) / hour ago (C) / in the cafeteria (D).
q.x: When a specific time in the past is mentioned, the simple past tense should be used instead of the present perfect. 'Finished' is correct, but 'I finished' is required without 'have'.

q.q: Neither the teacher nor the students (A) / was aware of the (B) / change in the schedule (C) / for the upcoming week (D).
q.x: When two subjects are joined by 'neither/nor', the verb must agree with the closer subject. Since 'students' is plural, the verb should be 'were' instead of 'was'.

q.q: Not only the IT department is responsible for data security, (A) / but every single employee also needs to be (B) / vigilant regarding potential phishing attempts (C) / and suspicious email attachments (D).
o: Not only the IT department is responsible for data security,
but every single employee also needs to be
q.x: The correlative conjunction 'not only... but also' requires parallel structure. The sentence should begin 'The IT department is not only responsible...', placing the verb before the conjunction.

q.q: The police have reported that the suspect (A) / was seen fleeing the scene (B) / along with a accomplice (C) / who was wearing a red hoodie. (D)
q.x: The error is in part C. The indefinite article 'an' should be used before 'accomplice' because it begins with a vowel sound. 'A' is used only before consonant sounds.

q.q: She has been working (A) / in this organization (B) / since five years (C) / without any complaints (D).
q.x: For a duration of time, 'for' is used instead of 'since'. 'Since' is used for a specific point in time.

q.q: Between the two options presented for the load balancer, (A) / the latter is definitely more preferable (B) / than the former due to its superior (C) / throughput and latency metrics (D).
o: Between the two options presented for the load balancer,
the latter is definitely more preferable
than the former due to its superior
q.x: The word 'preferable' already carries the meaning of 'more desirable'. Using 'more' before 'preferable' is a redundant construction known as a double comparative.

q.q: Hardly had I (A) / reached the station (B) / than the train (C) / started to move (D).
q.x: The correlative conjunction for 'Hardly' is 'when', not 'than'. 'Than' is used with 'no sooner'.

q.q: The project was delayed because the hardware components, (A) / despite being ordered months ago, (B) / was stuck at the customs office (C) / for an unforeseen duration (D).
o: The project was delayed because the hardware components,
was stuck at the customs office
q.x: The subject 'hardware components' is plural. Therefore, the verb 'was' is incorrect and must be changed to 'were'.

q.q: The committee is divided in their opinions (A) / regarding the implementation of the new policy (B) / which has caused a lot of friction (C) / among the members. (D)
q.x: The error is in part A. When a collective noun like 'committee' is divided, it acts as a plurality, necessitating the use of 'are divided' instead of 'is divided'. Furthermore, the pronoun 'their' is used correctly to reflect this plurality.

q.q: If I was you (A) / I would not have (B) / accepted the offer (C) / given the circumstances. (D)
q.x: In hypothetical situations or unreal conditions, 'were' is used instead of 'was' with the subject 'I'. It should be 'If I were you'.

q.q: No sooner did he see (A) / the tiger than (B) / he ran away (C) / in great fear. (D)
q.x: There is no grammatical error in this sentence. 'No sooner' is correctly paired with 'than', and the verb inversion is correct.

q.q: Each of the participants (A) / are expected to bring (B) / their own stationery (C) / to the workshop (D).
q.x: The subject 'Each' is singular, so it requires a singular verb. 'Are' should be replaced with 'is'.

q.q: The furniture in this (A) / new office are (B) / made of high-quality (C) / teak wood (D).
q.x: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb. 'Are' should be replaced with 'is'.

q.q: Despite of his (A) / hard work, he (B) / could not secure (C) / the top position (D).
q.x: 'Despite' does not take the preposition 'of'. You should either use 'Despite his hard work' or 'In spite of his hard work'.

q.q: It is high time (A) / we should take (B) / some concrete steps (C) / to curb the inflation. (D)
q.x: The phrase 'It is high time' is followed by the past subjunctive (simple past). Therefore, it should be 'we took', not 'we should take'.

q.q: One of the most (A) / intelligent boys (B) / that has ever lived (C) / in this village is Rahul. (D)
q.x: The relative pronoun 'that' refers to 'boys' (plural), so the verb must be plural. It should be 'that have ever lived'.

q.q: Neither the lead developer nor the project managers were aware (A) / that the migration strategy suggested by the consultant (B) / were fundamentally flawed and likely to cause (C) / systemic downtime during peak hours (D).
o: Neither the lead developer nor the project managers were aware
that the migration strategy suggested by the consultant
were fundamentally flawed and likely to cause
q.x: The subject of the clause is 'migration strategy', which is singular. Therefore, the plural verb 'were' must be replaced with the singular verb 'was' to maintain subject-verb agreement.

q.q: Neither the manager (A) / nor the employees (B) / was aware of (C) / the sudden change in schedule. (D)
q.x: In 'neither/nor' constructions, the verb must agree with the closer subject. Since 'employees' is plural, the verb should be 'were' instead of 'was'.

q.q: The committee, comprising of several senior architects and software engineers, (A) / has reached a consensus regarding the implementation (B) / of the new microservices architecture (C) / throughout the entire organization (D).
o: The committee, comprising of several senior architects and software engineers,
has reached a consensus regarding the implementation
q.x: The verb 'comprise' means 'to consist of'. It should not be followed by 'of'. Either use 'comprising' alone or replace it with 'composed of'.

q.q: Each of the software testers have been instructed (A) / to log all bugs encountered (B) / during the stress testing phase (C) / in the centralized tracking dashboard (D).
o: Each of the software testers have been instructed
q.x: When 'Each' is the subject of the sentence, it is grammatically singular. Thus, 'have been' should be 'has been'.

q.q: One of the most intelligent scientists (A) / who has ever worked (B) / in this research institute (C) / have resigned today. (D)
q.x: The error is in part D. The subject of the sentence is 'One', which is singular. Therefore, the verb 'has' should be used instead of 'have' to maintain subject-verb agreement.

q.q: Not only the students but also the teacher (A) / were present in the auditorium (B) / to witness the historic event (C) / organized by the club. (D)
q.x: The error is in part B. When using 'not only... but also', the verb must agree with the subject closest to it. Since 'the teacher' is singular, 'was' should be used instead of 'were'.

q.q: Neither of the two candidates (A) / who have been shortlisted (B) / for the vacancy are (C) / competent enough to handle the project. (D)
o: competent enough to handle the project
q.x: The subject is 'Neither', which is singular. Therefore, the verb must be 'is' instead of 'are'.

q.q: Each of the participants (A) / were asked to submit (B) / their feedback forms (C) / by the end of the session. (D)
o: by the end of the session
q.x: The subject 'Each' is singular and requires a singular verb. 'Were' should be replaced with 'was'.

q.q: Hardly had he arrived (A) / at the station (B) / then the train (C) / started to depart. (D)
q.x: The correlative conjunction for 'hardly' is 'when', not 'then'. The sentence should read 'when the train'.

q.q: The number of applications received for the post (A) / are significantly higher (B) / than what we initially (C) / anticipated last month. (D)
q.x: The error is in part B. 'The number of' is treated as a singular unit, so it takes a singular verb. 'Is' should be used instead of 'are'. If it were 'A number of', the verb would be plural.
